podcasts.name: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: British Folk Scene Figure
podcast.body: Elliott moved to Britain where his status as an "actual authentic American" made him a major figure in the British folk and related skiffle scenes. "before going over to Britain, where his status as an actual authentic American had meant he was one of the major figures in the British folk scene and the related skiffle scene."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Guthrie Imitator
podcast.body: Like Bob Dylan, Ramblin' Jack Elliott was a middle-class Jewish man who reinvented himself as a "Woody Guthrie copy." He was an "apprentice" of Guthrie, living with him and learning extensively. "Ramblin Jack Elliott was already doing the Guthrie imitation thing."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 97: "Song to Woody" by Bob Dylan

podcast.title: Topic Records Contract
podcast.body: Alan Lomax, while in the UK, helped Elliott secure a contract with Topic Records, a folk label connected to the Communist Party of Great Britain. "Alan Lomax, who had moved to the UK temporarily to escape the anti-communist witch hunt, had got Elliott to contract with Topic Records"
